impact:
T-009's description states the existing packaging contract already enforces installation with lifecycle scripts disabled. It does not: tests-ts/contract/packaging.contract.mjs installs the packed tarball into a scratch prefix without --ignore-scripts, and the four-package-manager script-disabled matrix named in the v0.1 plan row remains unimplemented.

The consequence is scoped and concrete: T-009 is next in the work queue, and an implementer reading this treats acceptance criterion 7 as already satisfied and skips building the check, leaving the "no lifecycle scripts" gate resting on a test that never ran with scripts disabled.

Note T-008 round 14 strengthened the sibling check in spikes/lifecycle.test.mjs to scan the whole production dependency tree (npm ls --omit=dev) for preinstall/install/postinstall hooks and for native builds via binding.gyp/gypfile — previously it only read the root manifest, so a dependency declaring its own install hook passed. That closes the manifest half of the gate; the actual script-disabled INSTALL across npm/pnpm/yarn/bun is still unbuilt and belongs to T-009.

Suggested fix: correct the claim, and state that lifecycle-script-disabled installation is new work required by criterion 7.

Found by codex review during T-008 round 14.
title: T-009 claims lifecycle-script-disabled install coverage that does not exist yet
